To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD44 and the ERM family of proteins are localized in the stratum intermediate and papillary layer cells of mouse enamel organs, and that their distribution changes during amelogenesis.
the CD44 molecule and the ezrin, radixin, and moesin (ERM) protein family are involved in cytoskeletal arrangement and cell-cell interaction of the cells that constitute the enamel organ.

CD44 and the ERM family were concentrated in the region at the contact between preameloblastic cells and the stratum intermediate at the differentiation stage, in the microvillus of the cells in stratum intermedium in the secretory stage, and in the microvillous region in the papillary layer in the maturation stage of amelogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunohisto-chemical localization of CD4 and the ezrin-radixin-moesin (ERM)-family of actin binding protein in mouse enamel organ.

the immunolocalization of cell surface adhesion molecule, CD44, and the ERM family in mouse enamel organ during amelogenesis, using confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
the immunolocalization of cell adhesion molecules and cytoskeleton-related proteins in ameloblasts and enamel organs of mouse incisors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD44-Ezrin-Radixin-Moesin system is involved in cytoskeletal organisation of the cells in stratum intermedium.
the CD44 molecule is a cell adhesion molecule that plays a role in the regulation of the cytoskeleton and the organization of the actin filaments in ameloblasts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD44 and ERM family proteins play important roles in the cytoskeleton organization in the stratum intermediate cells, which is a key cell in the enamel organ.
the ERM family and CD44 are associated with the cytoskeleton and cell–cell interaction of ameloblast cells and the stratum intermediate and the papillary cells of the mouse enamel organ.

the CD44-Ezrin-Radixin-Actin Filament System is involved in cell-cell interaction between preamelblasts and the Stratum Intermedius, as well as in the cytoskeleton of the cells of Stratum Intermedium and the Papillary Layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that CD44 is expressed on all cells of the mouse enamel organ, but that its distribution is differentially expressed on the different cell types.

the CD44-Ezrin-Radixin-Moesin (ERM)-actin system plays an important role in cell-to-cell interaction between pre-ameloblasts and stratum intermedium (SI) cells, and in the organization of the cytoskeleton of SI cells.
CD44, a receptor for hyaluronic acid, is expressed in the stratum intermediate and papillary layer cells, and the ERM family of cytoskeletal proteins is localized in these cells.
